note: Presets are saved parameter sets for the same animation; they do not count as additional animations. All content is fictional and illustrative; relationships, their kinds, the premise text and its status are supplied by the author. A relation is never drawn as causation unless the author supplies the causal kind. No conclusion is drawn.

presets.name: baseline-illustrative
presets.description: Fictional shed key: fact and conclusion on the walk line with the argument as written (fact, then conclusion) arcing over the empty gap; the intermediate premise, supplied as LEFT UNSTATED, lies in the layer beneath the gap; the tracer goes fact → hinge links → premise → conclusion and the premise enlarges. Gathered, it stays beneath the gap and the hinges fold back home.

presets.name: contrast-or-alternative
presets.description: Substantive alternative: a fictional library return whose argument STATES its premise; a supplied communication link from the magnifier and a different traversal order and focus (the hinge links). Gathered, the printed card rises into the gap and both hinges latch it into the walk.

params.facts: The blue umbrella was left at the library desk
params.rules: Items left at the desk go to lost property at closing
params.conclusion: The umbrella went to lost property
issues: Did the desk close at the usual time that day?

relationships.label: the premise takes up the fact

presets.name: long-labels-stress
presets.description: Long fact, premise and conclusion texts, long component labels and relation captions, two issues and two assumptions.

params.facts: The only key to the garden shed was found in the inside pocket of Jo’s winter coat the next morning
params.rules: Whoever is holding the only shed key the next morning is the person who locked the shed the night before
params.conclusion: Jo is the person who locked the garden shed on the night before the key was found
issues: Who else could have opened or locked the shed that evening without the key?
Was the coat left unattended in the hall overnight?
assumptions: There is only one key and no other way to lock the shed
The coat was not lent to anyone that evening
